summary:
TN ASTROPULSE space-venture – Interactive Space Mission Simulator

TN ASTROPULSE space-venture is an interactive space mission simulation game that gives players a chance to experience what goes into planning a real space mission. Instead of just reading about rockets, planets and satellites, players get to make their own mission decisions and learn through different challenges.

Players can choose their destination, such as the Moon, Mars or Earth orbit, and decide the purpose of their mission, whether it is for research, communication, navigation or other space activities.

They can then explore real-world launch vehicles and learn about their specifications, features, components, capabilities and estimated costs. Based on their choices, players must answer technical questions, manage their mission budget and complete various challenges before getting ready for launch.

Our idea is to bring space science and gaming together in a way that makes learning more interesting and easier to understand. By using real-world space data, interactive challenges and problem-solving activities, TN ASTROPULSE helps students discover how space missions work and understand the science and engineering behind them.

Through this project, we hope to encourage more students to explore space, develop scientific curiosity and discover the exciting possibilities of aerospace technology.
details:
Space-venture – Project Details

Project Overview

Space-venture is an interactive space mission planning and simulation game where players get to experience what it is like to be a real space mission designer. The idea is to take players beyond simply learning about rockets and planets and let them make their own mission decisions. From choosing a destination and selecting a rocket to designing a spacecraft, managing a budget and preparing for launch, players experience the different stages involved in planning a space mission using real-world space technology.

1. Mission Planning

The game starts with a main menu, a Start Mission option and a short set of instructions to help players understand how to play. Players can choose one of three destinations: the International Space Station (ISS), the Moon or Mars.

After selecting a destination, they decide what kind of mission they want to carry out, such as sending humans into space, deploying satellites, conducting research, communication, navigation, cargo delivery or space exploration. Each choice introduces different mission requirements and challenges.

2. Real-World Rocket Selection

One of the main features of the game is the opportunity to explore around 20–30 real-world rockets and launch vehicles.

Each rocket will have its own information page showing its name, model, first launch year, specifications, capabilities, propulsion system, fuel type, major components, payload capacity and special features.

Players can explore and compare rockets such as Falcon 9, Space Launch System (SLS) and Atlas V. Through this, they can understand that not every rocket is suitable for every mission and that the choice of launch vehicle depends on the mission's destination, payload and requirements.

3. Satellite and Spacecraft Design

Based on the selected mission, players will explore different types of satellites and spacecraft. They can learn about their purposes, important components, onboard instruments, communication systems and power sources.

The game also helps players understand how different payloads are selected and why spacecraft need specific equipment to complete their missions successfully.

4. Budget Management and Technical Challenges

Planning a space mission is not only about choosing a rocket; it also involves managing resources and costs.

In this stage, players receive a mission budget and must make decisions based on the estimated costs of the selected rocket, spacecraft and other mission requirements.

After completing the budget challenge, they face five technical questions covering topics such as rocket engineering, propulsion systems, satellite technology, orbital mechanics and mission planning.

Each question comes with a short explanation so that players can understand the science behind their answers rather than simply knowing whether they are correct or incorrect.

5. Orbital Science and Mission Simulation

Before launching the mission, players get an introduction to the science behind space travel. They explore concepts such as orbital paths, altitude, velocity, travel time and the different trajectories required to reach the ISS, Moon or Mars.

The game then takes players through the major stages of a space mission, helping them understand how a spacecraft moves from launch towards its intended destination.

Finally, players reach the mission-readiness stage, where they can review their decisions and experience a simulated launch.

Tools, Data and Technology

The game is being developed using the Godot game engine. To make the learning experience scientifically meaningful, the project uses information from reliable space-science sources, including NASA mission records, NASA Open APIs, JPL Horizons and Solar System Dynamics resources. And ai tools like chatgpt , gemini

and languages like html , css ,java script

These sources help us refer to real rockets, spacecraft, planetary information and orbital data while developing the game.

Innovation and Intended Impact

What makes Space Mission Designer interesting is that it brings several aspects of space exploration together in one interactive experience. Instead of just reading about rockets, satellites and planets, players get to make decisions, face challenges and understand the reasons behind different engineering choices.

By combining real-world rocket information, spacecraft design, budget management, technical questions and orbital science, the game turns space education into a hands-on learning experience.

Our aim is to make space technology easier and more interesting to understand, especially for students who are curious about space but may not know where to begin. We hope this project encourages scientific thinking, creativity and an interest in aerospace engineering while helping players experience the challenges involved in designing a space mission.
